prompt: Five students from Class A scored $70, 75, 80, 85, 90$ on a test. Five students from Class B scored $60, 78, 80, 82, 100$. Which comparison is correct?

choices.label: Class B has a higher mean than Class A
The classes have the same mean and median, but Class B is more spread out
The classes have the same mean, but Class A has the higher median
Class A is more spread out because its scores change by the same amount each time

hint: Compare center first (mean and median), then spread (range or how far scores sit from the middle).

hints.text: Compare center first (mean and median), then spread (range or how far scores sit from the middle).

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: $4, 5, 6$ and $1, 5, 9$ both have mean $5$ and median $5$, but the second set is far more spread out. Same check here with five scores.
Class A: mean $= \frac{400}{5} = 80$, median $80$. Class B: mean $= \frac{400}{5} = 80$, median $80$. Now compare the ranges.
Range A $= 90 - 70 = 20$; range B $= 100 - 60 = 40$. Same center, B more spread: choice B.

explanation: Class A: $70 + 75 + 80 + 85 + 90 = 400$, so the mean is $80$; the middle value is $80$.
Class B: $60 + 78 + 80 + 82 + 100 = 400$, so the mean is also $80$; the middle value is also $80$.
Spread differs: Class A ranges $20$ points, Class B ranges $40$ points and its extreme scores sit farther from $80$. Choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Distances from the center
steps: Class A distances from 80: $10, 5, 0, 5, 10$ — average distance 6.
Class B distances from 80: $20, 2, 0, 2, 20$ — average distance 8.8.
Bigger typical distance means more variability, so Class B is more spread out.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why choice D is a trap
steps: Evenly spaced scores look "orderly", but spread is about how far values are from the center, not about a pattern.
Class A's farthest scores are 10 points from the middle; Class B's are 20 points away.
So Class B, not A, has the greater spread.
